purpose: Before and after on the benchmark suite that /table shows: for each student, the within-run B answer (before) and the self-improvement loop of MC-104 (after), on the six main-v1 datasets with local gold. The student writes every final answer. These items were used to design the router (MC-90 to MC-95), so the comparison is descriptive of the familiar benchmark numbers, not held-out evidence; the held-out evidence is MC-104.

items.source: the frozen vi-multimodel main-v1 manifest data/vi_multimodel_v1/main_v1.json, the items and prompts of the /table runs
items.vmlu_dev: the VMLU dev row is MC-104's (same loop, same students); it is reported beside, not re-run

arm_meaning.B: the frozen main-v1 prompt, byte for byte the prompt of the /table runs
arm_meaning.S: the campaign step-by-step template of data/diagnostic_prospective_v1/prompt_templates_v1.json, as in MC-90 to MC-104

qwen.route: the campaign transport of data/diagnostic_prospective_v1/protocol.json (IEC endpoint, Responses API, temperature 1.0, 4,096 output tokens), for every arm except the multiple-choice B

probe.confidence: the probability of the parsed letter, renormalized over the letters the item offers (run_mc_calibration_eval.letter_probs and offered_letters); missing when fewer than two offered letters are visible or the option block cannot be read

loop.agreement: router v2's normalized-answer-v1 (diagnostic_router.answers_agree): both parsed answers non-empty and equal; multiple choice compares the letter, reading the exact-match normalization of the vi-reading-v3 prediction

multiple_choice.qwen: MC-104: round 1 keeps B-r1 when its probe confidence is at least 0.80; round 2 keeps B-r1 when S-r1 agrees with it; round 3 takes the majority of S-r1 to S-r3
multiple_choice.mimo: MC-104: round 1 keeps B-r1 when B-r1 and B-r2 agree; round 2 keeps S-r1 when it agrees with one of them; round 3 takes the majority of S-r1 to S-r3
multiple_choice.threshold_source: MC-104's registered rule on 660 VMLU valid items of MC-94 and MC-95, which are among this card's VMLU valid items

loop.reading: both students: round 1 keeps B-r1 when B-r1 and B-r2 agree; round 2 keeps S-r1 when it agrees with one of them; round 3 takes the majority of S-r1 to S-r3 by normalized answer, a tie to the earliest, the earliest attempt of the winning answer final; an empty answer casts no vote, and with no answer S-r1 is final
loop.final_answer: always one of the student's own logged answers

reference.source: web/data/benchmark-reports.json, the published /table numbers (MC-83, MC-85); different route and settings, so a reference only

analysis.score: multiple choice: accuracy by the frozen letter parser; reading: token-F1 under vi-reading-v3 (primary), exact match beside, vi-reading-v2 beside both

policies.always_vote: the majority of S-r1 to S-r3 as in round 3

primary.test: multiple choice: exact two-sided McNemar of the loop against always_B; reading: the mean paired token-F1 difference with a two-sided sign-flip p-value (20,000 resamples, seed 7)
primary.met: Holm p below alpha and the loop scores higher

descriptive: loop minus always_S and always_vote minus always_S, mean paired difference with a percentile bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples, seed 7)
mean reported tokens per item of each policy; the loop pays for every request its rounds use, two B answers in round 1 except Qwen's multiple choice
the /table number of MC-83 and MC-85 beside each dataset
MC-104's VMLU dev row beside the six datasets
